items.fix: Use one form everywhere: "Wait at least 4 hours before the next dose." Put it in every "How often" cell, e.g. "Up to 4 times in 24 hours. Wait at least 4 hours between doses." For the 2 to 3 month row: "1 dose. If needed, 1 more dose at least 4 hours later. No more than 2 doses in total."
items.impact: Readers who take the text literally may think "4 to 6 hours" has an upper limit and be unsure whether waiting longer is wrong. Someone using the table alone, by screen reader cell by cell or by scanning, gets the daily count but not the minimum gap, so doses could be given too close together.
items.problem: The gap between doses is given as "4 to 6 hours" in one place and "at least 4 hours" in another. The "How often" column gives only the number of doses per day, never the gap, which appears only in the note after the table.
items.where: dosing.html, table row "2 to 3 months (after vaccinations)": "a second dose after 4 to 6 hours if needed"; the warning note: "Leave at least 4 hours between doses"; the "How often" cells for the other rows: "Up to 4 times in 24 hours"

items.fix: On both pages add a short "Who to contact" section listing a pharmacist, NHS 111 (phone 111 as a tel: link, plus 111 online and the relay or BSL options), and 999 for emergencies. In the Easy Read give each its own row and picture, with one sentence on when to use it.
items.impact: A worried carer is told to "talk to a doctor" with no way to do it, which in practice means waiting for a GP appointment or not asking at all. Easy Read readers, people with learning disabilities, anxiety or cognitive impairments, and Deaf users needing a text or relay route get fewer ways to get help.
items.problem: Neither page says how to reach help: no phone number, no NHS 111 option, no out-of-hours route and no link. The full page offers "doctor or pharmacist", but the Easy Read drops the pharmacist, who is often the quickest person to ask without an appointment.
items.where: dosing-easy-read.html: "If you are worried, talk to a doctor." and "If your baby is under 3 months old, talk to a doctor first."; dosing.html: "speak to a doctor or pharmacist", "Speak to a doctor if your child still has a fever after 3 days, or you are worried."

items.fix: Add plain explanations at first use, e.g. "A **dose** is the amount of medicine you give at one time." "A **syringe** is a plastic tube for measuring medicine. It has no needle." Show a picture of each.
items.impact: A reader who does not know a "dose" is a measured amount given once cannot follow the timing advice. A reader who does not know what an oral syringe looks like may use something else to measure.
items.problem: Hard words are not explained the first time they appear. "Dose", the key idea of the page, is never explained. "Syringe" is neither explained nor shown, because the picture next to it is a spoon (sym/spoon.png). The page has no word explanations.
